newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: Singapore shares end mixed, economic data awaited.
newsitem.headline: Singapore shares end mixed, economic data awaited.

text.p: Singapore shares ended mixed on Tuesday with investors hesitant to commit themselves ahead of economic data from the United States and Singapore this week, dealers said.
"This data question is going to keep people out until the news is fully digested," said one dealer at a local firm.
Singapore's Straits Times Industrials Index closed down 10.94 at 2,124.29, a slight recovery from an earlier fall to 2119.21.
Singapore's sometimes rocky relationship with neighbouring Malaysia was seen as another factor.

Dealers said a Malaysian cabinet meeting on Wednesday discuss Singapore Senior Minister Lee Kuan Yew's criticism of a Malaysian state -- for which he issued an unreserved apology -- could bring reprisals for Singapore firms.
"Wednesday will be important for two reasons -- the U.S. data and the Malaysian cabinet meeting," one dealer said.
Volume reflected the hesistancy with 197.5 million shares traded, producing 195 gainers against 185 losers.
Gainers were led by North Borneo Timber, up Singapore $0.75 to S$9.90. Losers were headed by Great Eastern Life down S$0.60 to S$23.50.
